cards.text: Jesus is teaching beside the sea again, and the crowd gets so big that He gets into a boat and sits in it while everybody crowds the shore. He teaches them many things in parables. Friend, my bakery has NEVER been so busy I had to teach from a boat.
Jesus opens with one word: "Listen!" A farmer goes out to sow his seed, and just like my sprinkles, it doesn't all land in one place.

cards.question: Some of the farmer's seed falls along the path. What comes and eats it up?

cards.text: Some seed falls on rocky ground. There's not much soil there, just a thin layer over the rock.

cards.question: The seed on the rocky ground comes up slowly because the soil is so shallow.
When the sun rises, the seedlings on the rocky ground are scorched and wither. Why?

cards.text: Other seed falls among thorns. And those thorns grow up right alongside the seedlings.

cards.question: In the farmer's field, the thorns grow up and ___ the seedlings, and they yield no crop.

cards.text: Still other seed falls on good soil. After the path, the rocks AND the thorns, this farmer is three batches deep and needs a win.

cards.question: What happens to the farmer's seed on the good soil?

answers.text: It grows and produces a crop
It sprouts and then withers away
It grows but never forms a head

cards.question: All the seed on the good soil produces the exact same size crop.

cards.text: Jesus wraps it up with, "He who has ears to hear, let him hear." No explanation. He just leaves it on the counter like a cookie with no label.
As soon as Jesus is alone with the Twelve, His closest disciples, and the others around Him, they come to Him with a question.

cards.question: When Jesus is alone with the Twelve and those around Him, what do they ask Him about?
Jesus tells the Twelve that the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to them. How is everything expressed to those on the outside?

cards.text: Then Jesus quotes the prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 6:9-10), about people who are "ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding".

cards.question: In the words Jesus quotes, what might happen otherwise, if those people did perceive and understand?

answers.text: They might turn and be forgiven
They might go and tell others

cards.text: Jesus is still alone with the Twelve, and He asks, "Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?" Friend, that's me with a brand new oven manual: if I can't get past page one, page forty is NOT happening.

cards.question: Jesus starts explaining the parable. What does the farmer sow?
Some people are like the seeds along the path. What happens as soon as they hear the word?

answers.text: Satan comes and takes it away
They argue it out of their heads

cards.text: Satan, the devil, snatches the word just like those birds on the path. Then come the rocky-ground people, who hear the word and at once receive it with joy.

cards.question: The rocky-ground people receive the word with joy. Why do they last only a season?
When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, the rocky-ground people fall away slowly over many years.

cards.text: Then the thorns. These people hear the word too, and friend, I know what it's like to get buried: I spent YEARS under takeout menus in a junk drawer.

cards.question: Jesus names three things that come in and choke the word in the thorny-ground people. Which one is on His list?
In the thorny-ground people, the word still produces a small crop.

cards.text: Worries, wealth and wanting other things crowd in until the word is choked out, like a phone buzzing through a conversation until you forget what anybody said. Then, at last, the good soil.

cards.question: The good-soil people hear the word. What happens next?

answers.text: They receive it and produce a crop
They receive it and keep it hidden
They study it but never share it

cards.text: Jesus keeps going. He asks, "Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed?"

cards.question: Jesus asks if anyone brings in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed. Where does He say it goes instead?
Right after the lamp, Jesus says some things that are concealed will stay hidden forever.

cards.text: Then that line again: "If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear." And He goes on: "Pay attention to what you hear."

cards.question: Jesus says that with the measure you use, it will be measured to you. What else does He say?

answers.text: Even more will be added to you
Nothing more will be added to you
Less will be given back to you

cards.question: Jesus says whoever has will be given more. What about whoever does not have?

answers.text: Even what he has will be taken away
He will be given a little to start
He will be given exactly what he needs

cards.text: Jesus has another one: the kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground. Seeds AGAIN. Friend, I named six stations and six toppings after my kids, so I RESPECT a man with a theme.

cards.question: As the man sleeps and wakes night and day, he knows exactly how the seed sprouts and grows.

cards.text: He sleeps, he wakes, he sleeps, he wakes, and the seed grows anyway. That's me staring through the oven window like my staring is doing ANYTHING.

cards.question: In this parable about the kingdom of God, what produces the crop?

answers.text: The man working night and day

cards.question: In what order does the man's crop grow?
As soon as the grain is ripe, the man swings the ___, because the harvest has come.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, "To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?"

cards.question: What does Jesus compare the kingdom of God to next?
Jesus calls the mustard seed the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.

cards.text: But once that mustard seed is planted, it doesn't stay small. Friend, I came out of a 25-cent bin, so I am ROOTING for this little guy.

cards.question: What does the tiny mustard seed grow to be?

answers.text: The largest of all garden plants
A small bush in the corner

cards.question: The mustard plant puts forth great branches. What nests in its shade?

cards.text: Birds AGAIN! Back on the path they ate the seed, and now they're moving into what a seed grew into. With many such parables, Jesus spoke the word to them, "to the extent that they could understand."

cards.question: Jesus doesn't tell them anything without using a parable. What does He do privately with His own disciples?

answers.text: He tells them even more parables
He asks them to explain to Him

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The joke calls the farmer's seed 'three batches deep.' That mixes baking with the farm scene instead of keeping one separate everyday image. The text also has seed falling in different places while he sows, not three separate failed tries.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'This farmer ... needs a win' states a feeling as fact. The parable gives the farmer no reaction.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the quote, 'No explanation.' and the counter line. It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 1 already told the baker that Jesus taught the crowd 'many things in parables.' That gives away the answer to how everything is expressed to those on the outside. The card needs a different question about verse 11, for example what has been given to the Twelve.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has 8 multiple choice cards, 3 true or false and 0 fill in the blank, so multiple choice dominates by a wide margin. Stops 1 and 3 are also heavily multiple choice (6, 2 and 1 each) and use the same mix.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The right answer 'The deceitfulness of wealth' sounds like Bible wording. The wrong answers 'The opinions of neighbors' and 'The length of the workday' sound modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card says 'wealth' crowds in and chokes the word. Mark 4:19 says 'the deceitfulness of wealth,' not wealth itself. The card also mostly retells verse 19 after cards 8 and 9 already covered it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke teases Jesus for repeating seeds ('Seeds AGAIN ... I RESPECT a man with a theme'), which makes Jesus' teaching the target of the humor. The card is also 3 sentences and isn't the opening card.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card comes after card 2 already covered verse 27 and just retells it (he sleeps, he wakes, the seed grows). It doesn't move the passage forward.
'It doesn't stay small' rules out the wrong answer 'A small bush in the corner' on card 11.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks what 'nests' in the shade. Foxes and sheep don't nest, so the verb points straight to the birds.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Birds AGAIN!', the path callback, and the verse 33 line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
